anchor_text: <Dialogue speaker="Fr. Andrew Stephen Damick" time="01:07">Good evening, Giant Killers and Dragon Slayers. You are listening to the Lord of Spirits podcast, and my co-host [[Father Stephen]] De Young is with me from Lafayette, Louisiana, and I am [[Father Andrew]] Stephen Damick in Amaus, PA.</Dialogue>
<Dialogue speaker="Fr. Andrew Stephen Damick" time="08:17:632">Right. Right.</Dialogue>

<Dialogue speaker="Caller" time="09:57:40">Hi Fathers, I have a question on the garments of skin in contrast to the fig leaves. Growing up, I was taught that the fig leaves were Adam and Eve's way of trying to cover for their sins through works, as if it's some kind of parallel to the whole of the Old Testament and the law. Whereas the garments that [[God]] made were some kind of uh appeasing of his anger and a sense of justice in that an animal had to be killed and blood had to be shed in order for uh salvation to to truly take effect if you like. I've listened to enough of the whole Council of [[God]] to know that this kind of shorthand idea of appeasing [[God]]'s wrath is uh certainly we'll say not giving the full picture. So in short, what are the fig leaves? What's going on with the fig leaves versus the garments of skin? Thank you very much.</Dialogue>
<Dialogue speaker="Fr. Stephen De Young" time="02:19:157">Thank you. Good night. And [[God]] bless you.</Dialogue>
